title: Write the discriminating test
prompt: Implement `static int FirstDistinct(int[] nums)` — the first element that differs from all previous ones (nums[0] never qualifies); -1 when none. Then the graded part: your own test group must include a case distinguishing "first distinct" from "any distinct" and a case for the all-equal array.

tests.name: normal
tests.hint: The reference implementation and its discriminating cases.

tests.name: discriminator
tests.code:
Cj.Eq(Solution.FirstDistinct(new[] { 2, 2, 2, 9, 1 }), 9, "first distinct, not min distinct");
Cj.Eq(Solution.FirstDistinct(new int[0]), -1, "empty");
tests.hint: 9 qualifies before 1 — an "any distinct" bug would answer 1.
